title: Travis Barker - Wikipedia
notes: Travis Landon Barker, born 14 November 1975, Fontana, California. His mother gave him his first kit at four; lessons from five with Michael Mai, 'who would expose young Barker to many different playing styles'; trumpet, then piano. At Fontana High School the drum set in the jazz ensemble and the snare drum in the marching band; 'military and jazz rhythms', but 'attracted to the driving rhythms of hip-hop and punk rock'. The Aquabats (from 1996, as 'Baron Von Tito'); filled in for Scott Raynor in Blink-182 in 1998, learning the 20-song set in 45 minutes, and joined that year; filled in for Josh Freese in the Vandals. Box Car Racer (2002), the Transplants with Tim Armstrong (from 2002; Rolling Stone: 'punk rock's first superstar drummer'), +44 with Mark Hoppus (2005–2006), TRV$DJAM with DJ AM (2008); the 2008 plane crash; Give the Drummer Some (2011). Favourite drummers: Animal from the Muppets (his first hero), John Bonham, Alex Van Halen, Tommy Lee and Danny Carey; Buddy Rich the greatest of all time (Vevo, 2016); Van Halen's 'Jump' the first song he learned.

title: David Ciauro, 'Travis Barker', Modern Drummer, September 2012
notes: 'I grew up on punk, rap, metal, and thrash, so of course I want to play all those styles.' 'I like to break the rules and knock down barriers between genres.' 'Quick 32nd-note singles between my hands and right foot' for the fills on Give the Drummer Some; everything tracked on his OCDPs, no triggers. Records to a click when the drums go first. Taught privately with the Aquabats and early in Blink-182: 'Ilan Rubin, who plays in Angels & Airwaves now with Tom DeLonge, is a former student.' Working on open-handed playing, leading with the left; 'I've never played double bass. I always wanted to be a single-bass player and to take my single kicks to new levels.' His first tattoo for his mother, who told him on her deathbed to keep playing; the tattoos as 'job stoppers' to rule out a plan B.

title: 'Drum Analysis: What Makes Travis Barker So Special?', Drumhead Authority
notes: Marching rudiments with odd accents on the snare are 'almost the Blink-182 signature bridge' (Going Away to College, All the Small Things, Bored to Death), or moved to the ride (The Party Song, What's My Age Again?'s intro and bridge). Dynamics by the instrument rather than by playing softer: Feeling This's chorus drop closes the hat and trades snares for the cowbell. Adam's Song's verse 'a loopy tom part accented by splashes, crashes, and choked hi-hats'. Moving between half time, normal time, double time and punk time (the snare on every 'and'), Dumpweed the example. A side snare with a thinner head for the verses of Stay Together for the Kids. Kits: Orange County Drum & Percussion, acrylic and maple, a 6.5x14 snare, a 10- or 12-inch tom, a 16-inch floor tom, a 22-inch bass drum; DW hardware, a DW 5000 pedal. Zildjian: 14-inch A Quick Beat hats, 18- and 19-inch A Custom crashes, an 18-inch Oriental China, a 21-inch Sweet Ride ('that really defined ping ... for playing fast punk songs like The Rock Show'), a 10-inch splash. Single strokes, hard and fast, with accents.

title: 'Drum heroes week: Travis Barker', Rhythm / MusicRadar, 19 September 2014
notes: On the marching band: 'I love that stuff! It still comes out in my playing.' Warms up on a practice pad for two hours, traditional grip: 'That's not even how you're going to be playing.' 'With Blink, we're always to a click. I love, love playing to a click.' 'I change my fills every night. I improvise.'

title: Enema of the State - Wikipedia
notes: Released 1 June 1999, MCA; produced by Jerry Finn; his first record with the band. 'Unlike Raynor, whose playing emphasized traditional double-time punk rhythms, Barker brought exceptional technical ability and a broader musical vocabulary.' He arranged the songs but, as a hired musician, had no writing credit; the drums tracked at Mad Hatter Studios, North Hollywood.

title: Take Off Your Pants and Jacket - Wikipedia
notes: Released 12 June 2001, MCA; produced by Jerry Finn, who 'was very fond of Barker's drum parts, which the other musicians found unconventional and "algebraic"'. Drums recorded in 'two or three days', from memory, largely in one take; the first record he tracked to a click. Arrangements worked out at his Famous Stars and Straps warehouse.

title: Blink-182 (album) - Wikipedia
notes: The untitled album, released 18 November 2003, Geffen; produced by Jerry Finn; recorded through 2003, first in a rented house in Rancho Santa Fe. 'That's by far my favorite album we did.'

title: What's My Age Again? - Wikipedia
notes: The lead single from Enema of the State (April 1999), the band's first with him. 158 bpm. 'Barker's drumming incorporates syncopated kick patterns and intricate fills'; he based the drum rhythm on Jawbreaker's 'Boxcar'.

title: All the Small Things - Wikipedia
notes: The second single from Enema of the State (September 1999), a Modern Rock number one; 150 bpm; 'a steady mid-tempo drum beat from Barker'. Over time, he said, playing it became tiresome.

title: Adam's Song - Wikipedia
notes: The third single from Enema of the State (March 2000); 136 bpm. Drummerworld: 'one of the most creative beats of his career', the same basic beat through the verses. The first bar: the kick and the splash on the downbeat, the ride's bell on the 'and' of 2, an open hat ringing a full count on 3. Retired in 2009 after the death of DJ AM.

title: The Rock Show - Wikipedia
notes: The lead single from Take Off Your Pants and Jacket (7 May 2001); its arrangement worked out at the Famous Stars and Straps warehouse; Wikipedia gives 182 bpm. Played by him and Hoppus in +44.

title: First Date (Blink-182 song) - Wikipedia
notes: The second single from Take Off Your Pants and Jacket (24 September 2001); written mostly by DeLonge; worked out at the Famous Stars and Straps warehouse.

title: Stay Together for the Kids - Wikipedia
notes: The third single from Take Off Your Pants and Jacket (4 February 2002); 72 bpm. It grew from a jam between him and DeLonge; before leaving to tour with another band he gave them a drum concept, 'tight, restrained drums influenced by hip-hop' in the verses against 'a considerably wider drum sound' in the choruses. Finished a day before the album went to be mixed.

title: Feeling This - Wikipedia
notes: The lead single from the untitled album (6 October 2003), the first song recorded for it; 173 bpm. His drum part 'super in respect to John Bonham'; it began as a faster drum 'n' bass track whose groove he imitated on open hats; the opening kick triplets after 'Good Times Bad Times'; the cowbell in the chorus first a joke. Engineer Ryan Hewitt: 'four distinct drum sounds created by old school tape editing'.

title: I Miss You (Blink-182 song) - Wikipedia
notes: The second single from the untitled album (2 February 2004); 111 bpm. Acoustic instruments, 'a brushstroked drum loop': he answered Hoppus's bassline with a pattern on brushes and persuaded the band to loop it rather than develop a more dynamic part, its repetition 'reminiscent of dance music'. Written by DeLonge, Hoppus and Barker.

title: 'Travis Barker Blink 182 Soundcheck 01 (Original)', YouTube r5JbZGwVuyY, uploaded 27 May 2009
notes: Four minutes of him alone at the kit on an arena stage, playing 'Down' (the upload's description). Frames read at 0:08 to 3:52: shirtless, his arms, chest and back covered in tattoos; dark hair in a short mohawk, the sides shaved; clean-shaven; grey-khaki cargo trousers. A metal-finish kit with chrome hardware, the bass drum's white front head with the OCDP logo and three ports, Zildjian cymbals. The date of the soundcheck is not given.
